name: Federal Republic of Central America 1823–1839 AD
description: The Federal Republic of Central America was formed in 1823 after seceding from the First Mexican Empire, uniting former Central American provinces into a liberal federal state. Deep internal divisions, regional rivalries, and conflicts between liberal and conservative forces led to civil wars and the gradual withdrawal of its member states, resulting in the federation’s legal dissolution by 1841.

name: Trinidad and Tobago 1962–Present
description: Trinidad and Tobago gained independence from the United Kingdom in 1962. The country initially remained a Commonwealth realm before becoming a republic in 1976. Its economy developed around oil and natural gas resources, making it one of the most industrialized Caribbean states. The nation maintains a stable parliamentary system and plays an important economic and cultural role in the Caribbean.

name: Republic of Barbados 1966–Present
description: Barbados gained independence from the United Kingdom in 1966 after more than three centuries of British colonial rule. It remained a Commonwealth realm until 2021, when it became a parliamentary republic. Known for political stability and a strong tourism and services economy, Barbados plays a prominent diplomatic and cultural role in the Caribbean.

name: State of Grenada 1974–Present
GovernmentType: constitutional monarchy (1974–1979), Revolutionary socialist government (1979–1983), Parliamentary constitutional monarchy (1983–Present)
description: Grenada gained independence from the United Kingdom in 1974 as a Commonwealth realm. A socialist revolution in 1979 established the People's Revolutionary Government under Maurice Bishop. Internal conflict and a U.S.-led intervention in 1983 ended the revolutionary regime. Democratic elections in 1984 restored the parliamentary constitutional monarchy that continues to govern the country today.

name: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines 1979–Present
description: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines gained independence from the United Kingdom in 1979. It became a parliamentary constitutional monarchy within the Commonwealth, retaining the British monarch as head of state. Since independence the country has maintained stable democratic institutions and an economy based on agriculture, tourism, and regional Caribbean trade.

name: Dominica 1978–Present
description: Dominica gained independence from the United Kingdom in 1978. Unlike many Caribbean states, it became a parliamentary republic at independence while remaining in the Commonwealth. The country has maintained democratic institutions and an economy based on agriculture, tourism, and regional trade within the Caribbean.

name: Saint Lucia 1979–Present
description: Saint Lucia gained independence from the United Kingdom in 1979. It became a parliamentary constitutional monarchy within the Commonwealth, retaining the British monarch as head of state. Since independence the country has maintained democratic governance and an economy based on tourism, agriculture, and regional Caribbean trade.

name: Antigua and Barbuda 1981–Present
description: Antigua and Barbuda gained independence from the United Kingdom in 1981. The country became a parliamentary constitutional monarchy within the Commonwealth, retaining the British monarch as head of state. Since independence it has maintained democratic institutions and an economy centered on tourism, offshore finance, and regional Caribbean trade.

name: Saint Kitts and Nevis 1983–Present
description: Saint Kitts and Nevis gained independence from the United Kingdom in 1983. It became a federal parliamentary constitutional monarchy within the Commonwealth. The federation grants significant autonomy to Nevis, whose constitution includes a legal mechanism allowing the island to secede through a referendum requiring a two-thirds majority.

name: Jamaica 1962–Present
description: Jamaica gained independence from the United Kingdom in 1962 after withdrawing from the West Indies Federation. It became a parliamentary constitutional monarchy within the Commonwealth. Since independence the country has maintained democratic institutions and a mixed economy based on tourism, mining, agriculture, and services.

name: Bahamas 1973–Present
description: The Bahamas gained independence from the United Kingdom in 1973. It became a parliamentary constitutional monarchy within the Commonwealth, retaining the British monarch as head of state. The country developed a stable political system and an economy strongly based on tourism, offshore finance, and maritime services.

name: Belize 1981–Present
description: Belize gained independence from the United Kingdom in 1981, ending its period as the colony of British Honduras. It became a parliamentary constitutional monarchy within the Commonwealth. The country maintains democratic institutions and a diverse society influenced by Caribbean, Central American, and British cultural traditions.

name: Cuba 1902–Present
description: Cuba became independent in 1902 following the end of U.S. military occupation after the Spanish–American War. In 1959 the Cuban Revolution led by Fidel Castro overthrew the previous government and established a socialist state. Cuba has since operated as a one-party socialist republic.

name: Unified Hispaniola under Haiti 1822–1844
description: Haiti emerged in 1804 after the Haitian Revolution defeated French colonial rule, creating the first Black republic. In 1822 President Jean-Pierre Boyer unified the island of Hispaniola by occupying the former Spanish colony of Santo Domingo. Haitian administration lasted until 1844 when Dominican rebels declared independence, ending Haitian control of the eastern part of the island.

name: Haiti 1804–Present
description: Haiti was founded in 1804 after the Haitian Revolution defeated French rule, creating the first Black republic. In 1822 Haitian forces unified the island of Hispaniola by occupying Santo Domingo. Dominican independence in 1844 ended this control. A treaty signed in 1929 later established the modern international border between Haiti and the Dominican Republic.

name: Dominican Republic 1844–Present
description: The Dominican Republic was founded in 1844 after a revolt against Haitian rule ended the unification of Hispaniola under Haiti. The new state experienced wars with Haiti and later a brief reannexation by Spain between 1861 and 1865. A bilateral treaty in 1929 finally fixed the modern border between the Dominican Republic and Haiti.
